item.title: He Posed As His Victim Online To Lure Other Women
item.description: Serial killer John Edward Robinson used Suzette Trouten’s email account to conceal her disappearance and steer her friend toward another of his aliases. Investigators found Trouten’s body on his Kansas property in 2000. His capital murder conviction and death sentence were upheld in 2015.

item.title: Baby Brianna’s Death Changed New Mexico Law
item.description: Five-month-old Brianna Lopez died in 2002 after prolonged abuse inside her New Mexico home. Her mother, father and uncle were convicted in connection with her death. Public outrage later helped drive a state law imposing far tougher penalties for intentional child abuse resulting in death.

item.title: Her Final Film Was Released After Her Murder
item.description: Ten-year-old Judith Barsi voiced Anne-Marie in All Dogs Go to Heaven before she and her mother were murdered by her father in 1988. The animated film became Judith’s final role and was released posthumously the following year.

item.title: She Followed A Murder Trial Hours Before Her Son Died
item.description: Corie Walsh is charged with first-degree murder in the September 2026 death of her 2-year-old son, Barrett. Prosecutors say she had been closely following the Lindsay Clancy trial and discussing it just hours earlier. Walsh has pleaded not guilty, while her attorneys say she was experiencing a psychotic episode.

item.title: His Google Searches Came Hours After Karoline’s Death
item.description: Royce Moser is charged with killing his 18-year-old girlfriend, Karoline Heintz, in August 2026. Investigators testified that hours later he searched questions about murder and being controlled by a “demon.” He and his mother have been ordered to stand trial.
